## R Markdown

## Step 1 Check CONDA on the HPC and your Storage
Log into the HPC and run:
```{bash}
conda --version
```
If it prints a version, move on to step two, otherwise redo the Miniforge installation from Rachel's tutorial

Check storage with:
```{bash}
quota -s
df -h ~
```



## Step 2 Make a STAR Environment
```{bash}
conda create -n acer_star \
    --override-channels -c conda-forge -c bioconda --strict-channel-priority \
    star samtools pandas multiqc
conda activate acer_star
STAR --version && samtools --version | head -1
```
Write down the versions so you will have them when preparing a manuscript

## Step 3 get your trimmed reads onto your HPC
First make a destination for your reads in the hpc
```{bash}
mkdir -p ~/acer_survival/trimmed_reads
```


To move from your laptop to the hpc, use rsync

```{bash}

rsync -avhz  path/to/local/<target file>/ mxg3231@hpcr8o2rnp.uta.edu:/home/mxg3231/acer_survival/trimmed_reads/

```
If your data is in the coral immune server, log in there and run the rsync

## Step 4 get your reference genome and annotation on to the HPC
Should be in FASTA and GTF format
Make directory in HPC
```{bash}
mkdir -p ~/acer_survival/reference
```

Use rsync again
```{bash}
rsync -avhz  path/to/local/<target file>/ mxg3231@hpcr8o2rnp.uta.edu:/home/mxg3231/acer_survival/reference
```

## Step 5 Upload BASH scripts to HPC

Copy these scripts into and save as .sbatch with the corresponding file names
config:
```{bash}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Edit these paths once; every script sources this file.
export PROJ=${PROJ:-$HOME/acer_survival}
export READS_DIR=/path/to/trimmed_reads          # folder with *_fp_R1.fq.gz / *_fp_R2.fq.gz and *_fastp.json
export GENOME_FA=/path/to/Acer_genome.fasta
export GTF=/path/to/Acer_genes.gtf
export STAR_INDEX=$PROJ/ref/star_index
export OUT=$PROJ/star_out
export SAMPLES=$PROJ/samples.tsv
export THREADS=8

# Activate the conda environment (tools: STAR, samtools, python+pandas)
set +u   # conda's activate scripts can trip over 'set -u'
source "$HOME/miniforge3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh"   # change if Miniforge lives elsewhere
conda activate acer_star
set -u
mkdir -p "$PROJ" "$PROJ/logs" "$OUT" "$(dirname "$STAR_INDEX")"

```
00_make_samplesheet:
```{bash}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Builds samples.tsv from the trimmed reads and records the read length for STAR's --sjdbOverhang.
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/config.sh"

printf "sample\ttimepoint\tr1\tr2\n" > "$SAMPLES"
for r1 in "$READS_DIR"/*_fp_R1.fq.gz; do
  s=$(basename "$r1" _fp_R1.fq.gz)
  [[ "$s" == PBL_* ]] && continue   # March 2025 samples excluded for now; remove this line to include them
  r2="$READS_DIR/${s}_fp_R2.fq.gz"
  [[ -f "$r2" ]] || { echo "MISSING R2 for $s" >&2; continue; }
  # ASSUMPTION: BL_* = October 2024 (peak bleaching), PBL_* = March 2025. Confirm against metadata.
  case "$s" in PBL_*) tp=Mar2025;; BL_*) tp=Oct2024;; *) tp=unknown;; esac
  printf "%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n" "$s" "$tp" "$r1" "$r2" >> "$SAMPLES"
done
echo "Samples: $(tail -n +2 "$SAMPLES" | wc -l)"
tail -n +2 "$SAMPLES" | cut -f2 | sort | uniq -c

# Original (pre-trim) read length from fastp JSON -> max over samples
python3 - <<'EOF' > "$PROJ/read_len.txt"
import glob, json, os
L = []
for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(os.environ["READS_DIR"], "BL_*_fastp.json")):
    d = json.load(open(f))
    L.append(int(round(d["summary"]["before_filtering"]["read1_mean_length"])))
print(max(L))
EOF
echo "Max read length: $(cat "$PROJ/read_len.txt")  (sjdbOverhang will be this minus 1)"

```

01_star_index:
```{bash}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#SBATCH --job-name=star_index
#SBATCH -p short
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=48G
#SBATCH --time=04:00:00
#SBATCH --output=logs/star_index_%j.out
#SBATCH --error=logs/star_index_%j.err
set -euo pipefail
source "${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR:-$(dirname "$0")}/config.sh"   # submit from the star_pipeline folder

READ_LEN=$(cat "$PROJ/read_len.txt")
OVERHANG=$((READ_LEN - 1))

# STAR recommends min(14, log2(GenomeLength)/2 - 1); matters a lot for small genomes
GENOME_LEN=$(awk '!/^>/{n+=length($0)} END{print n}' "$GENOME_FA")
SA=$(awk -v n="$GENOME_LEN" 'BEGIN{v=log(n)/log(2)/2-1; if(v>14)v=14; printf "%d", v}')
echo "Genome length: $GENOME_LEN  SAindexNbases: $SA  sjdbOverhang: $OVERHANG"

# If STAR errors on the GTF (no exon/gene_id), see README note: your GTF may use different attribute names.
STAR --runMode genomeGenerate \
     --runThreadN "$THREADS" \
     --genomeDir "$STAR_INDEX" \
     --genomeFastaFiles "$GENOME_FA" \
     --sjdbGTFfile "$GTF" \
     --sjdbOverhang "$OVERHANG" \
     --genomeSAindexNbases "$SA" \
     --outFileNamePrefix "$PROJ/ref/index_"

```

02_star_align:
```{bash}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#SBATCH --job-name=star_align
#SBATCH -p short
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=32G
#SBATCH --time=06:00:00
#SBATCH --array=1-48%10
#SBATCH --output=logs/star_align_%A_%a.out
#SBATCH --error=logs/star_align_%A_%a.err
# Resize the array to your sample count, e.g.:
#   sbatch --array=1-$(($(wc -l < samples.tsv)-1))%10 02_star_align.sbatch
# Test on one sample first:  sbatch --array=1 02_star_align.sbatch
set -euo pipefail
source "${SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR:-$(dirname "$0")}/config.sh"   # submit from the star_pipeline folder

LINE=$(sed -n "$((SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID + 1))p" "$SAMPLES")
[[ -n "$LINE" ]] || { echo "No sample for task $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID"; exit 0; }
IFS=$'\t' read -r SAMPLE TP R1 R2 <<< "$LINE"

SDIR="$OUT/$SAMPLE"
mkdir -p "$SDIR"
if [[ -f "$SDIR/${SAMPLE}.ReadsPerGene.out.tab" && -f "$SDIR/${SAMPLE}.Log.final.out" ]]; then
  echo "$SAMPLE already done, skipping"; exit 0
fi

TMP=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/star_${SAMPLE}_$$
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT   # STAR requires that --outTmpDir does not exist yet

STAR --runThreadN "$THREADS" \
     --genomeDir "$STAR_INDEX" \
     --readFilesIn "$R1" "$R2" \
     --readFilesCommand zcat \
     --outFileNamePrefix "$SDIR/${SAMPLE}." \
     --outTmpDir "$TMP" \
     --outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate \
     --outSAMattributes NH HI AS nM \
     --quantMode GeneCounts \
     --outFilterMultimapNmax 20 \
     --outFilterMismatchNoverReadLmax 0.04 \
     --alignSJoverhangMin 8 \
     --alignIntronMax 100000

# samtools index "$SDIR/${SAMPLE}.Aligned.sortedByCoord.out.bam"   # uncomment if samtools is loaded
echo "Finished $SAMPLE"

```

03_merge_counts:
```{bash}
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Merge STAR ReadsPerGene.out.tab files into one gene x sample counts matrix (for DESeq2)
and summarise mapping rates from Log.final.out.

Usage: python3 03_merge_counts.py <star_out_dir> <output_prefix>
STAR's ReadsPerGene has 3 count columns: 2 = unstranded, 3 = read 1 matches gene strand,
4 = read 1 opposite to gene strand. The right column is the one with the most assigned reads
across samples; it is chosen automatically and the evidence is printed so you can sanity-check.
"""
import glob, os, re, sys
import pandas as pd

star_dir, prefix = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
files = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(star_dir, "*", "*.ReadsPerGene.out.tab")))
if not files:
    sys.exit("No ReadsPerGene files found")

cols, totals = {}, {2: 0, 3: 0, 4: 0}
for f in files:
    s = os.path.basename(f).replace(".ReadsPerGene.out.tab", "")
    df = pd.read_csv(f, sep="\t", header=None, index_col=0)
    genes = df[~df.index.str.startswith("N_")]
    cols[s] = genes
    for i, c in enumerate([1, 2, 3], start=2):
        totals[i] += genes[c].sum()

best = max(totals, key=totals.get)
print("Assigned reads by strandedness column (2=unstranded, 3=forward, 4=reverse):", totals)
if sorted(totals.values())[-1] < 1.5 * sorted(totals.values())[-2]:
    print("NOTE: columns 2 and the best stranded column are similar -> library is likely unstranded; using column 2.")
    best = 2
print(f"Using column {best}")

mat = pd.DataFrame({s: d[best - 1] for s, d in cols.items()})
mat.index.name = "gene_id"
mat.to_csv(f"{prefix}_counts.tsv", sep="\t")
print(f"Wrote {prefix}_counts.tsv  ({mat.shape[0]} genes x {mat.shape[1]} samples)")

# Mapping QC
rows = []
for f in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(star_dir, "*", "*.Log.final.out"))):
    s = os.path.basename(f).replace(".Log.final.out", "")
    txt = open(f).read()
    def g(key):
        m = re.search(re.escape(key) + r"\s*\|\s*([\d.]+)", txt)
        return float(m.group(1)) if m else None
    rows.append({"sample": s,
                 "input_reads": g("Number of input reads"),
                 "uniq_map_pct": g("Uniquely mapped reads %"),
                 "multi_map_pct": g("% of reads mapped to multiple loci")})
qc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
qc["assigned_to_gene"] = [mat[s].sum() if s in mat else None for s in qc["sample"]]
qc.to_csv(f"{prefix}_mapping_qc.tsv", sep="\t", index=False)
print(f"Wrote {prefix}_mapping_qc.tsv")
print(qc.describe().loc[["min", "mean", "max"]].round(1).to_string())

```

Save all of these to a folder on your laptop named star_pipeline

rysnc to the HPC
```{bash}
rsync -avhP /mnt/c/users/Mason/Downloads/star_pipeline mxg3231@hpcr8o2rnp.uta.edu:/home/mxg3231/acer_survival/star_pipeline

```
## Step 6 edit config.sh on the HPC
cd to the star_pipeline folder
```{bash}
nano config.sh
```

Change these to match actual file names:
READS_DIR=/home/<netID>/acer_survival/trimmed_reads
GENOME_FA=/home/<netID>/acer_survival/ref/genome.fasta
GTF=/home/<netID>/acer_survival/ref/annotation.gtf

Ensure the miniforge path is correct as well

## Step 7 build the sample sheet
```{bash}
mkdir -p logs
bash 00_make_samplesheet.sh
```

## Step 8 build the STAR index
```{bash}
sbatch 01_star_index.sbatch
squeue -u $USER
tail logs/star_index_*.out
```

Ensure ~/acer_survival/ref/star_index now contains files like SA and Genome

## Step 9 test on one sample
```{bash}
sbatch --array=1 02_star_align.sbatch
```

Open ~/acer_survival/star_out/<Sample_name>.Log.final.out and check Uniquely mapped reads %
60-90% ideal, if lower it may be due to an incorrect reference or symbiont reads BLAST can check for this

## Step 10 run all samples
```{bash}
N=$(( $(wc -l < ~/acer_survival/samples.tsv) - 1 ))
sbatch --array=1-${N}%10 02_star_align.sbatch
```

%10 runs 10 at a time. Check progress with squeue -u $USER. Resubmitting is safe, because finished samples are skipped. Look at failures in logs/star_align_*.err.

## Step 11 merge the counts

```{bash}
python3 03_merge_counts.py ~/acer_survival/star_out ~/acer_survival/acer
```

Gives you acer_counts.tsv and acer_mapping_qc.tsv which you should save to your laptop via rsync to use for DESeq analysis
